o1.biggest_strength: It cleanly separates what the data proves from what still needs checking, then turns that into a practical plan with owners, stop rules and a usable scorecard.
o1.biggest_mistake: It slightly overstates certainty on paid economics by assuming repeat-order value and margin match first orders, and one scorecard target ('flow share of email revenue') is left relative rather than numeric.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Tighten the paid payback logic with one clearer sensitivity range for repeat value/margin and give every scorecard line a hard numeric target.

o2.biggest_strength: It is ruthlessly owner-minded: it ranks moves in contribution terms, gives stop/go thresholds, and directly tackles the two real leaks—Meta and linen—while restoring the switched-off CRM engine.
o2.biggest_mistake: A few of the contribution estimates and formula-based sizing assumptions are more speculative and harder to verify from the brief, which makes the financial precision feel less solid than the confidence of the plan.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Keep the ranking structure, but simplify and de-risk the impact math so every number clearly traces back to the brief without layered assumptions.

reason: Both are strong and clearly built on the data, but Output 2 feels more like the plan I could run with a board and team tomorrow because it ranks the moves in one owner metric, sets firmer decision lines, and is sharper about what happens each week.
